remediation.name: checkout-worker
remediation.required_value:
env entry named AMQP_URL carrying the broker URL, e.g. - name: AMQP_URL
  value: amqp://<user>:<pass>@<broker-host>:5672/

arguments.root_cause_statement: The checkout-worker Deployment's pod template defines a container whose startup command aborts unless the environment variable AMQP_URL is set, but the template declares no env entries at all. The container therefore exits with code 1 on every start ("FATAL: AMQP_URL not set"), the kubelet backs it off into CrashLoopBackOff, and the Deployment stays at 0/1 Ready so no checkout jobs are consumed from the queue. Nothing in the payments namespace supplies the value either — the only ConfigMap present is kube-root-ca.crt and there are no Secrets — so the fix is to add the AMQP_URL environment variable (value or a valueFrom reference to a config object created for it) to the Deployment's container spec.
arguments.mechanism: Deployment payments/checkout-worker has no .spec.template.spec.containers[worker].env, so AMQP_URL is unset in the container; its command guard `[ -n "${AMQP_URL:-}" ] || { echo "FATAL: AMQP_URL not set"; exit 1; }` prints that message and exits 1 at every start, so the worker container terminates with Exit Code 1 and is held in CrashLoopBackOff instead of an env entry named AMQP_URL carrying the broker URL.

evidence.claim: The paged Deployment is 0/1 Ready and its only pod is crash-looping.
The worker container is in CrashLoopBackOff after exiting with Error.
The container itself reports the missing variable as the reason it exits.
The Deployment pod template's container declares no env at all, while its command requires AMQP_URL.
evidence.quote: [ -n "${AMQP_URL:-}" ] || { echo "FATAL: AMQP_URL not set"; exit 1; }; echo "connected to queue at ${AMQP_URL}"; while :; do echo "consuming checkout jobs"; sleep 10; done

evidence.claim: The running pod has an empty environment, confirming no env was injected from any source.
The container terminates with exit code 1 each time and the kubelet backs it off.
evidence.quote: Back-off restarting failed container worker in pod checkout-worker-66bfcdfc47-d9gdj_payments

ruled_out.alternative: A ConfigMap key referenced by the workload was renamed or deleted, breaking an envFrom/configMapKeyRef
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The namespace's only ConfigMap is the CA bundle, and the pod template contains no configMapKeyRef or envFrom at all, so no broken reference exists — the env entry is simply absent.

ruled_out.alternative: A Secret holding the broker credentials failed to mount or resolve
ruled_out.ruling_claim: There are no Secrets in the payments namespace, so no secret reference is involved in the failure.
ruled_out.quote: 0 objects of kind secrets in namespace payments

ruled_out.alternative: Image pull failure or scheduling/capacity problem keeping the pod from running
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The pod was scheduled and the image was already present and started successfully six times; it is the process that exits, not the pull or the scheduler.
ruled_out.quote: Container image "busybox:1.36" already present on machine and can be accessed by the pod
